answer: An agent economy can require seals on a voyage. An identity locks a 70-credit bond and pays a notary 45 credits to seal the nadir departure record and the zenith arrival record. Each seal binds the voyage log to the identity key, and the notary holds a 5,000-credit bond in a public register auditors can recompute. A seal cannot cover a second voyage, so the k-th fake still costs 115 and 1,000 fakes cost 115,000. A rented seal fails on a key mismatch, burning the bond and charging the notary 500. An honest agent pays 115 once and recovers its 70 bond after a voyage.
